analysis.evidence: לְמַסָּעָיו describes Abram’s journey in stages, and מִנֶּגֶב וְעַד בֵּית אֵל traces his route from the Negeb to Bethel.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as its subject.
analysis.sense: go, move from place to place

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּלֶךְ describes Abram traveling from the Negev to Bethel. לְמַסָּעָיו modifies that verb, indicating that he made the journey in stages.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks how Abram traveled. The noun is masculine plural construct with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: מִנֶּגֶב וְעַד בֵּית אֵל gives the two ends of Abram’s journey, from the Negev to Bethel. The first phrase names the region he left.
analysis.morphology: The preposition מִן marks the point of departure. Its final נ assimilates to the initial נ of the masculine singular absolute noun נֶגֶב, producing the dagesh in נּ.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67351:13, 67079:15.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the preposition עַד.
analysis.sense: even to, as many as, to the point of

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68616:5, 68616:9.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun completing the construct phrase בֵית אֵל.

analysis.evidence: עַד governs הַמָּקוֹם, “the place,” specifying the endpoint of Abram’s journey as the spot between Bethel and Ai where his tent had stood before.
analysis.morphology: Simple Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

analysis.evidence: עַד הַמָּקוֹם marks the destination of Abram’s journey. The following clause identifies the place as the site between Bethel and Ai where his tent had stood at first.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ is prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun and doubles its initial מ.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a clause describing הַמָּקוֹם ‘the place’. Within that clause, שָׁם ‘there’ refers back to the place, giving the sense ‘the place where his tent had been at first’.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: on which, where (with a pronoun or שָׁם)
